newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy competition body approves supermarket deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy competition body approves supermarket deal.

text.p: Italy's competition watchdog said on Friday it had approved a joint-venture between supermarket chains GS-Generali Supermercati and Standa to create a single food buying centre.

The anti-trust commission said in a regular weekly report that the deal between two of Italy's largest food retailers, agreed in November 1995, did not restrict competition on the wholesale and retail markets.
The deal will create a group called Supercentrale.
Standa is owned by Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest, while GS is controlled by Italian food retailer SME.
This in turn is jointly owned by the Benetton family's Edizione Holding, Luxottica's Leonardo Del Vecchio and Swiss Moevenpick Holding AG.
After a nine-month inquiry, the watchdog decided that Supercentrale did not have a particularly relevant position in the market and "many other centres have virtually the same market share."
It said there was therefore no risk that Supercentrale would have "such a dominant position that it can impose conditions and prices upon its distributors".
The watchdog also gave the go-ahead to a distribution deal which Supercentrale had signed with independent northern Italian store-chain Il Gigante.
